leverage.exposure: This is the item that outranks the rest. The Lienhart bid is live right now and Bernardo has not been sold, so the money behind it does not exist. If the seller accepts before Georg acts, the balance goes sharply negative - and a negative balance when the matchday locks scores zero for the entire matchday, not a penalty but a total loss. Unwinding it would then take both funding sales in quick succession. Pulling the bid removes the exposure outright and is the safest of the four actions. The recommended plan never goes negative at any point in the sequence: the sale precedes the bid, and the bid is smaller than the proceeds. A three-buy variant that would score higher was enumerated and rejected on exactly this ground - it requires a forced sale inside a two-hour window after the auction resolves, and missing that window costs the whole matchday. That trade is not worth a coin-flip on a zero. Separately and just as urgent: the live Amoako listing is a hundred-point penalty waiting to happen the moment the squad drops to eleven. Pull it before selling Bernardo, not after.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is not a formation hole - every position is covered and three formations are legal. It is the quality of the fifth defensive slot. The two weakest men in the fielded eleven are both defenders, one a substitute who has not started this season and the other the player now flagged knocked-up, and between them they contribute a small fraction of what the other nine do. That is exactly the slot the board has just offered a fit, full-ninety starting left-back into, at a price the Bernardo sale covers on its own. Attack and midfield need nothing - the two forwards and the two leading midfielders are the squad's strength, and every attacker and midfielder on the board is either flagged, unproven, or priced worse per point than what is already owned.

verdict.headline: The plan changes, and the change is a reversal: pull the live Lienhart bid.
verdict.headline_short: The plan changes, and the change is a reversal: pull the live Lienhart
verdict.detail: The plan changes, and the change is a reversal: pull the live Lienhart bid. Nothing is wrong with Lienhart - he is fit and in Freiburg's probable eleven - but a minute before this run a better-value defender from the same club hit the board, and the arithmetic around him is different in a way that matters. Buying Lienhart is only affordable if Lokonga is sold as well, and swapping Lokonga out for Amoako inside the fielded eleven gives back more than Lienhart's extra points bring in. Buying Makengo instead needs only the Bernardo sale, keeps Lokonga on the pitch, leaves a spare body in the squad, and ends with a higher fielded total for materially less money. The order of operations is the whole job this run: pull the Amoako listing, pull the Lienhart bid, sell Bernardo, then bid Makengo. Do not improvise the sequence - two of those four steps exist purely to stop the squad falling to ten players or the balance falling below zero.

sell.reason: Bernardo, to the board at market value, and it is the gate on everything else. The sale stands but the reason for it has been corrected, and the correction is worth stating because this ledger has now flipped on him three times. The previous run said he was confirmed benched with Hranac holding left-back. That does not survive re-checking: this run fetched the same Ligainsider page with the same timestamp and got Bernardo in the eleven, and a second independent fetch got him in the eleven too. Three reads of one page, three answers. What actually settles it is Kickbase's own status text, which no previous run pulled - he is flagged Stricken, did not come through the Koeln away game unscathed, dated 31 August. That is an injury doubt, not a benching, and it is the opposite of what the ledger recorded. It also fits the one fact nobody disputes: he started at Koeln and was hooked just after the hour with a poor rating. So he is a doubt, not a write-off - but a doubt is worth selling here, because his market value has turned upward and the market has priced neither the flag nor the hook, and because at eleven players a fielded man who might not play is a fielded zero with no cover behind him. Do not report him as a confirmed injury; he is not on Ligainsider's injured-and-suspended table and his profile still reads fit. Amoako is also a sale, but strictly a later one - not until Makengo has actually landed.

THE EVIDENCE THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT is Kickbase's own status text, which no previous run pulled: get_player 1954 returns st 2, stl [2], stxt "Stricken - does not come through KOE (A) unscathed", dt 2026-08-31T14:40:12Z. That is an INJURY DOUBT arising from the Koeln away game, not a benching - the precise opposite of what Sr72ldn concluded, and it is first-party rather than a scraped graphic. It corroborates the one mechanical fact nobody disputes: in Koeln 3:2 Hoffenheim, 29.08.2026 he started at left-back and was HOOKED AT 53 MINUTES with a rating of 4.0 (sec 3268). SO THE CORRECT READ IS: not confirmed benched, not confirmed injured, but flagged knocked-up by Kickbase since 31.08 and pulled at half-time-plus-8 in the only match he has played. His ap 62 is a doubt, not an expectation. He is NOT on Ligainsider's Verletzte-und-Gesperrte table (checked 03.09.2026 - Hoffenheim has no entries at all) and his Ligainsider profile box reads green fit, so do NOT report him as a confirmed injury either. WHY SELL ANYWAY, AND THE CASE IS STRONGER THAN THE OLD ONE: (1) his mv has TURNED UP - mv 7.048.552, mvt 1, tfhmvt +160.481, sdmvt +218.838 - so the market has priced neither the st 2 flag nor the 53-minute hook. Selling a flagged player into a rising price is a seller's edge and it decays. (2) At 11 players there is zero spare, so a fielded man who might not play is a fielded ZERO with no bench cover - keeping him is not the safe option, it is the risky one. (3) THE MONEY IS THE POINT: this sale is the gate on the Makengo buy. Cash is 4.107.522 and the Makengo bid needs ~9.000.000; only this sale unlocks it. EXECUTE FIRST, AFTER PULLING THE AMOAKO LISTING: 12 -> 11 = 1GK/4DEF/4MID/2ATT which fills 4-4-2 legally, cash -> 11.156.074, and the run's whole plan is funded. Sell to the board at mv 7.048.552 - do not list him at a premium, there is no time and a st 2 flag will not clear one. REVERSAL: a source dated 03.09.2026 or later putting him in the Hoffenheim XI for the Dortmund home game AND the Kickbase st flag clearing to 0. The flag clearing alone is not enough, and neither is another Ligainsider read.

buy.reason: Jordy Makengo, Freiburg left-back, new to the board and listed at exactly market value. He is the cleanest buy this ledger has recorded. He started matchday one and played the full match at left-back, he is in Freiburg's probable eleven for Paderborn away, he is absent from the injured-and-suspended table, and his profile reads fit. The transfer risk that would normally kill a player linked away in the window is dead twice over - Monaco publicly withdrew on 29 August, and the German window has since shut, so he cannot leave before matchday two. He is a left-back, not a midfielder; the Ligainsider pitch graphic that suggests otherwise is a layout artefact and every other source agrees. The point that makes him beat Lienhart is not that he is the better footballer - per minute played, Lienhart is - it is that he is affordable on the Bernardo sale alone, so no second sale is forced, so Lokonga stays in the eleven. And the call is robust to the Bernardo question in both directions: if Bernardo is fit and starts, Makengo is still an upgrade on him; if Bernardo is knocked up and blanks, the upgrade is far larger. There is no version of this where it loses. On price, the calibration table is unambiguous about where the losing zone is - Georg has lost the same board auction twice bidding around nine per cent over market value while the winner paid thirty. Do not bid there again. Bid above both measured contested-board clearings but well short of the level that cost four million of overpay on Onyeka. The auction resolves a couple of hours before the lock, so there is time to raise: later runs should watch the offer count and push toward the winner's level if it climbs. Every other listing on the board is rejected and logged - the flagged ones on their status field alone, the manager asks on points per euro, and the rest as unknown quantities priced above a player with a verified full-ninety start.

Every manager ask on the board is priced above market value, so the mechanism a profitable flip needs is simply absent, and the measured instant-flip margins remain almost entirely negative. What the feed does show is two rivals doing it anyway, faster than ever: one bought a defender off the board at market value and relisted him seven minutes later at a double-digit premium, another did the same with a full-back inside twenty minutes.
